Sir,
I beg to report that at 4 p.m., on the 23-7-24,

position of the Chinese Naval boats there.

a mile beyond the Russian ships, and another one is lying
opposite the Woosung Creek, some considerable distance away.

先生，
谨此报告，本人于1924年7月23日下午4时，
前往吴淞，就三艘俄国巡洋舰及停泊在该处的
中国海军船只的位置情况进行查访。
中国巡洋舰“永绩”号（Yung Kyih）
正横停泊，距离俄国船只约两百码，位于河流同一侧，
朝向吴淞方向，其位置似乎能够很好地监视
所有船只。另有一艘鱼雷艇停泊在俄国船只后方约半英里处，
还有一艘停泊在吴淞口对面，相距相当远。
四名华籍巡捕仍驻守在码头执勤，
该码头正对巡洋舰。
先生，
您忠顺的仆人，

In,

I beg to submit with reference to observation kept
on the Kiangsu and Anhui Gunboats at Pootung.

At 10-30 a.m., 17-7-24, I visited the spot and found
the above mentioned gunboats lying off the Bund near the
Customs House. There were about twenty armed men on board,
and they appeared to be in a state of readiness. I was informed
that they were waiting for orders from their Commander.
I could not ascertain what these orders were, but it was
rumoured that they were going to take part in some military
operations. I also heard that they had been ordered to proceed
to Nanking. I could not verify this report, but it seemed
probable that it was true.

At 4-30 p.m., 17-7-24, I again visited the spot and found
that the gunboats had left. I was informed by a native policeman
that they had gone up the river. I could not ascertain where
they had gone, but it was rumoured that they had gone to
Nanking. I could not verify this report, but it seemed probable
that it was true.

At 10 a.m., on the 17-7-24, two native policemen, accompanied
by the local Sikhs, visited the boat and inquired of the O. I. C.
what he was doing there and what his business was. He replied
that he was a policeman, and the Native Police under the
impression that the O. I. C. was a River Policeman, left the
boat.

On the instructions of the A/D. C. I., the watch was
withdrawn, and the boat sent back to Shanghai at 6-30 p.m. on the
17-7-24.

armed and equipped, arrived and are quartered in a Chinese
Hospital, beside the Jetty, opposite the Cruisers, presumably to
prevent the landing of too large a number of Russians from the
Cruisers.

At 9-45 a.m., eighteen Russians attempted to come
ashore from the Cruisers, but were prevented by the Chinese
Police on duty at the Jetty; thereupon they returned to the ships.

and went towards Shanghai by train. At 1-30 p.m. four, also

Jetty.

REPORT ON Observation on Russian Cruisers at Woosung.

Made by D.S. Grubb. Forwarded by [Signature] Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

I beg to report that at 6.10 p.m., 13-7-24, C.D.C.
No.79 Tsok Sung, who was on observation duty at Woosung on
the three Russian Cruisers, reported to me at Yangtszepoo
Station, that at 5.30 p.m. 13-7-24, 26 Russians, all dressed
in soldiers' uniforms, came ashore from the three vessels, in
three small rowing boats. The C.D.C. followed these men to
Tsang Wo Fang (張華浜) Railway Station. About half of the
men were carrying small bundles and bags; and whilst on the
way to the Station, four of them sold several articles of
underclothing to a number of countrymen. At a small shop
beside the Station, one of the men changed one dollar and the
C.D.C. overheard the shop-keeper asking the Russians where
they were going. One of them answered in Chinese "To
Shanghai!"

All the 26 men, when the C.D.C. left, were waiting
at the Tsang Wo Pang Station. It was ascertained that a train
would leave for Shanghai at 7 p.m.

At 9.20 a.m., ten Russians came ashore and went to-
wards Woosung. At 4 p.m. seven men also came ashore and these
went to Tsang Wo Fang Railway Station, but it is unknown if
these men went to Shanghai.

At 2 p.m. three respectably dressed Chinese, accom-
panied by five Russians dressed in soldier's uniform came
from the direction of Tsang Wo Pang Station and went aboard
the vessels. At 5.30 p.m. the three Chinese had not come
ashore.

先生，

当时在吴淞对三艘俄国巡洋舰执行观察任务的
刑事侦缉处警员 (C.D.C.) 79号 Tsok Sung，
在杨树浦巡捕房向我报告称，1924年7月13日下午5时30分，
26名俄国人全部身穿军服，乘坐三艘小划艇
从三艘船只上岸。该刑事侦缉处警员跟随这些人
前往张华浜 (Tsang Wo Fang) 火车站。
大约一半的人携带着小包裹和袋子；在前往车站的途中，
其中四人向一些同乡出售了几件内衣裤。
在车站旁的一家小店里，其中一人兑换了一美元，
该刑事侦缉处警员听到店主问俄国人要去哪里。
其中一人用中文回答：“去上海！”

当该刑事侦缉处警员离开时，所有26人
都在张华浜车站等候。经查实，一列火车
将于晚上7点发往上海。

上午9时20分，十名俄国人上岸并前往
吴淞方向。下午4时，另有七人上岸，这些人
前往张华浜火车站，但是否去了上海尚不清楚。

下午2时，三名衣着体面的中国人，
在五名身穿军服的俄国人的陪同下，
从张华浜车站方向走来，并登上了船只。
下午5时30分，这三名中国人尚未上岸。

Further REPORT ON Observation on Russian Cruisers at Woosung.

Made by D. S. Grubb. Forwarded by L. Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

I beg to report with reference to observation kept on the three Russian Cruisers at Woosung.

C. D. C. 36 Tuh Piao, who was on observation duty at Woosung, reports that three native Policemen were stationed at the Jetty, almost opposite the three Russian vessels, from 6 a.m., 14-7-24.

Between 9 and 10 a.m., six Russians left the vessels, and proceeded by a small boat to Woosung where they attempted to dispose of an number of brown uniform overcoats, but were unsuccessful.

At 6-30 p.m., about forty Russians, wearing soldiers' uniforms, and accompanied by two men wearing civilian clothing, who also appeared to be Russians, came from the direction of Tsang Wo Road (蕰藻浜) Railway Station, and went aboard the Cruisers.

The two men in civilian clothing, appeared to be of some importance, as they were saluted by two Russians who were stationed at the Jetty, and proceeded first in a small boat, apart from the others, to the Cruisers.

At 6-40 p.m., 14-7-24, I visited Woosung, and at that time there were no Chinese Naval boats in the vicinity of the Russian vessels, but two are reported by C. D. C. Tuh Piao to be stationed at the mouth of the Huangpoo.

At 6-40 p.m., there were four armed native Policemen stationed at the Jetty opposite the Cruisers.

I am, Sir,
Yours obediently
D. S.

A/ D. C. I.

Sir,

With reference to the statement made by
Magistrate Dung to the effect that orders had
already been given for a Chinese gunboat and a
torpedo boat to be stationed in the vicinity of

measures had apparently been taken by the

the Military Governor but he had learnt that
the gunboat "Yung Chih" had specially been
despatched to Woosung on instructions from the
Military Governor and that a batch of about 30
Policemen had been sent from the Chinese Constabulary
to Woosung for the special purpose of intercepting
Russians when they are found landing and proceeding
in the direction of Shanghai. He said he was
quite surprised to hear such news and would
inform the Governor. Magistrate Dung telephoned

阁下，

关于邓知事声称已下令派遣一艘中国炮艇和一艘鱼雷艇驻扎在吴淞三艘俄国难民船附近的说法，卑职谨报告称，今日下午2时30分曾致电督军公署，因邓知事不在，卑职告知参谋长王幼农（Wong Yu Noong），并未在俄国船只周围部署此类警卫，且除军事路上的四名警察外，中国当局显然未采取任何预防措施。王先生答复称，他不太确定督军的指令，但他获悉，“永治”号炮艇已奉督军之命特别派往吴淞，且已从中华警察厅派遣一批约30名警察前往吴淞，专门用于拦截被发现登陆并向上海方向行进的俄国人。他表示听到此类消息颇感惊讶，并将告知督军。邓知事致电

pages.en:
at 5.30 p.m. and stated that on the evening
of July 14, shortly after our visit to the
Governor's yamen General Ho issued an order
to Admiral Ling of the Chinese Independent fleet,
Col Lu, the Chief of the Woosung-Shanghai
Constabulary, Inspector Chao of the Woosung
Police and the Commander of the 12th Regt
Woosung warning them of the situation and
directing them respectively to send soldiers,
sailors and policemen to keep a sharp lookout
to intercept Russians found landing and to
fire on them if any should attempt to force
their way to Shanghai. The Admiral has in
a letter to the Governor replied to the effect
that on July 15 he had sent the "Yung Chih" to
Woosung which is now lying at Wen Cho Pang 蕰草浜
about 300 yards from one of the Russian ships.
In addition there are the "Lieh Tsz" 烈字 and
"Sung Tsz" 辰字 torpedo boats and a number
of police boats anchoring at Chang Hwa Pang. 张华浜
A watch had also been placed on the Naval
Hospital where certain sick Russians were staying
In view of the foregoing measures and the
strict instructions already issued by the
Military Governor, Magistrate Dung did not
think it possible for any Russians to land
at Woosung and proceed to Shanghai. He added
pages.zh: 于下午5时30分，并称7月14日晚，在我们拜访督军公署后不久，何将军向中国独立舰队凌司令、吴淞-上海警察厅厅长陆上校、吴淞警察局赵督察以及吴淞第12团团长发出命令，警告他们注意局势，并分别指示他们派遣士兵、水手和警察严加监视，拦截发现的登陆俄国人，若有人试图强行进入上海，则向其开火。凌司令在给督军的回信中表示，他已于7月15日派遣“永治”号前往吴淞，该舰目前停泊在距其中一艘俄国船约300码的蕰草浜。此外，还有“烈字”号和“辰字”号鱼雷艇以及数艘警用艇停泊在张华浜。海军医院也有监视哨，某些患病的俄国人正住在那里。鉴于上述措施及督军已发布的严格指令，邓知事认为不可能有任何俄国人在吴淞登陆并前往上海。他补充说

that the gunboat "Chun Oo" 春玉 of the

Tsungming to watch the other Russian
ship (s.s."Elderado").

Shanghai, July 14 1924.

Sir,
I beg to report that acting under your
instructions I interviewed Magistrate Dung ( 邓 )
at 2.45 p.m. to-day at the Military Governor's yamen
and informed him that a demonstration was expected
to take place at the former Russian Consulate
between Russian factions and that in all probability
force would be resorted to by such people.
The Acting Commissioner of Police, therefore,
ordered me to convey this news to the Chinese
Military Authorities with a view to steps being taken
by them to prevent any incursion of men stationed
on the three Russian boats in Chinese waters passing
through Chinese territory into the International
Settlement.

Magistrate Dung replied that the Chinese
Authorities were fully aware of the situation and
that in connection therewith a conference,
at which General Ho, Mr. Hsu Yuen,( the Commissioner
of Foreign Affairs), S.K.Chen and Magistrate Dung
were present, was held at the Military Governor's
Yamen on Saturday afternoon July 12. At
the conference Mr. Hsu Yuen said that he had been
in receipt of numerous telegrams from Peking blaming
him for not having handed over or caused to be
handed over the former Russian Consulate to the Soviets

阁下，
卑职谨报告，遵照阁下指示，卑职于今日下午2时45分在督军公署会见了邓知事（邓），并告知他预计前俄国领事馆内俄国各派系之间将发生示威活动，且这些人很可能会诉诸武力。因此，代理警务处长命令卑职将此消息传达给中国军事当局，以便他们采取措施，防止停泊在中国水域三艘俄国船上的人员穿过中国领土进入公共租界。

邓知事答复称，中国当局完全了解局势，为此，何将军、外交特派员许沅（Hsu Yuen）先生、S.K. Chen 先生和邓知事于7月12日星期六下午在督军公署举行了一次会议。会上，许沅先生表示，他收到许多来自北京的电报，指责他未将前俄国领事馆移交或促使移交给苏维埃

pages.en:
2

in Shanghai. There were about eight "White Russians"
staying at the former Consulate who strongly protested to
the building being handed over and Mr. Hsu had
thus been placed in a difficult position. He had
sent his secretary to see Major Hilton Johnson and
ask for his assistance but the Acting Commissioner
of Police replied that it being a political dispute,
Police could not interfere. The Magistrate conveyed
the wishes of the Military Governor that he and
Hsu Yuen were anxiously expecting Police assistance.
I said that the Police would remain neutral so long
as the different parties in dispute would do
nothing detrimental to the peace.

As a precaution against the rumoured demonstration
Magistrate Dung stated the conference on Saturday
decided to order Col. Lu, the Chief of Woosung
and Shanghai Constabulary and Admiral Ling of the
Shanghai Admiralty to send policemen and sailors
to Woosung to take steps to prevent Russians

Made by D. I. Givens Forwarded by [签名] Director of Criminal Intelligence.

Sir,

Further to my report on Russian Affairs submitted
this morning, the party of Cossacks numbering thirty four
told Mr. V. Grosse, Deputy Commissioner for Russian Affairs,
on the morning of July 14 to close the building, and threatened
to do so themselves if he failed to comply within an hour.
A complaint to this effect was communicated to the Act. Commission-
er of Police who sent a party of about thirty armed men under
Capt. Barrett and Chief Inspector O'Toole to the premises. On
being assured that the men in the Bureau were unarmed and
that they did not contemplate violence, Capt. Barrett left and
withdrew the guard of Municipal Police, with the exception of
about six.

Nothing untoward happened until shortly before noon
when General Gleboff telephoned to Mr. V. Grosse to say that
armed Chinese were preventing people from boarding and leaving
the ships at Woosung. Gleboff suggested that, if the surveillance
continued, the men, who came ashore on July 13 in connection
with the observance of the French National holiday, would be
obliged to force their way back to the ships, and trouble would
result. He also referred to the possibility of a further batch
of a hundred men from the ships joining those already in the
Bureau for Russian Affairs.

In response to the announcement in the New Shanghai
Life about the registration of persons desirous of being
repatriated some fifty people visited the Bureau. These, with
the exception of a few, left again without transacting any business.

Sir,

Some thirty five representatives of the Russian
refugees on board General Gleboff's ships at Woosung called
at the Bureau for Russian Affairs about 10 a.m. July 5. They
interviewed Mr. V. Grosse and asked that he would either
make provision for their maintenance or accord them permission
to sell the ships. After negotiations lasting all day, the
deputies left at 7.30 p.m. after Mr. Grosse had arranged to
take a delegation of them the following day to interview
the Chinese Commissioner for Foreign Affairs. This arrangement

with the Commissioner they repeated their request that provision

to sell the ships. Finally it was agreed that the Commissioner

should permission be given for the sale of the ships. The terms
of these orders were communicated to the men from the ships
in the Bureau for Russian Affairs who, nevertheless, still
remained in the building where they were reinforced by the
arrival on July 13 of an armed party of their colleagues,
consisting of about twenty men.
